_doc: Score bible · volume 5 (the Major Arcana) — see README.md. Home E; pre-Sinkhole cards sit on E / A / B / C#, the late cards drift to the flat side (Bb F C Eb G D) and walk home through C# A B to E at the World. Recurring beds: tape hiss (Priestess), fluorescent ballast (diner / offices), riverboat-engine drone (boat / cathedral), cicadas (bungalow / the World). The Demon lives a half-step up, in F.

5.feel: Operator-noir warm: D'Ambrosio's at three in the morning, the Cathedral's hum, cassette decks and phosphor-green CRTs, a Gulf-Coast river always moving just outside. Twenty-two arcana, one deck — every cue is a small lit room with a machine breathing in the corner. The Sinkhole splits the volume: the early cards sit close to home (E and its neighbours) and are warm and populated; after the Wheel the keys drift flat and far and the rooms empty out, until the World walks back down to the river in E.

vol5_ch0.feel: 0 · The Fool. D'Ambrosio's before dawn: vibes and a Wurlitzer over the fluorescent ballast, brushes, a bell at the pass. Home key, open mixolydian — the leap hasn't been taken yet.

vol5_ch1.feel: I · The Magician. The Cathedral of Rust and Code: bowed metal, choir in the rafters, a riverboat engine under the floor and the demons bound in phrygian. The first dark turn.

vol5_ch2.feel: II · The High Priestess. Elicia's bungalow at dusk: cicadas through the screen, tape hiss, a slow broken beat, her sustained voice-tone. Relative-minor C# — inward, listening.

vol5_ch3.feel: III · The Empress. Nicola's riverboat dining room: strings and clarinet over the engine, the long table set. Lush but moored — pre-Sinkhole abundance with static at the edges.

vol5_ch4.feel: IV · The Emperor. Dante's helm above the dining room: the same boat, brass and a clock instead of the table's warmth. Minor, upright, counting down to what takes him.

vol5_ch5.feel: V · The Hierophant. The Sunday circuit — St Jude's, the bandstand, Table 17 — and RUST_CODE.BBS humming under it: organ and choir, then phosphor. Fifth-up B, the most public chapter.

vol5_ch6.feel: VI · The Lovers. The Roberts kitchen: a felt piano, marimba drips keeping time, the faucet nobody fixes. Bittersweet dorian, small and domestic.

vol5_ch7.feel: VII · The Chariot. Antonio's hot office above Ember & Ash: a motorik pulse under a losing window unit, brass that wants to go. The last forward motion before the wreck.

vol5_ch8.feel: VIII · Strength. A New Orleans bar in refrains: sax, Rhodes, upright, vinyl. The volume leaves home for the flat keys — Bb — and stays known rather than conquered.

vol5_ch9.feel: IX · The Hermit. The Graustark ruin-scape: wind through scrawled walls, one lonesome whistle, a lantern flame. Sparse D dorian — a single light raised.

vol5_ch10.feel: X · The Wheel. After the Sinkhole: a Houston law office, motion denied, fluorescent hum. Alberto's cello note turning over a noir walk in F minor — the wheel turns either way.

vol5_ch11.feel: XI · Justice. Office to design studio, the morning after: chamber strings in harmonic minor, a clock, the city. Exact, costly, fair.

vol5_ch12.feel: XII · The Hanged Man. Natalie's apartment after midnight: a trip-hop drag, celesta floating in lydian, incense and tape hiss. The world calmly upside down.

vol5_ch13.feel: XIII · Death. St. Jude's Mercy hospice: a hymn at the pace of a breathing machine, felt piano, choir far off. G major — nothing exempt, nothing cruel.

vol5_ch14.feel: XIV · Temperance. A Montreal apartment years on: a jazz trio in patient exchange, vibes answering piano, two cups. Moderate in every parameter on purpose.

vol5_ch15.feel: XV · The Devil. Jimmy Daigle under a wobbling ceiling fan: a swamp groove in G mixolydian with the Demon's half-step figure worked into the harmonica. The chains are loose; they stay on.

vol5_ch16.feel: XVI · The Tower. Elicia's command center gone to plaster: industrial at full fan load, fuzz and Reese in F phrygian, impacts. The loudest, coldest card.

vol5_ch17.feel: XVII · The Star. Graustark ruins under a shard-of-mirror moon: harp and bowed glass in D lydian, water poured, glass pings. The first light after the Tower.

vol5_ch18.feel: XVIII · The Moon. Five a.m. after the cards: a celesta lullaby in C# minor over crickets and a clock. The keys start walking home.

vol5_ch19.feel: XIX · The Sun. Café Olimpico in late May: nylon guitar, Wurlitzer and espresso clatter in A major. Six years of Tuesdays — the warmest, plainest cue in the volume.

vol5_ch20.feel: XX · Judgement. The hush over the ruins shatters: post-rock that builds from wind to full band, brass calling, B (the dominant of home).

vol5_ch21.feel: XXI · The World. Minstral's Green by the rusting steamship: a bayou porch tune in E major, flute carrying John's apron phrase back to where the Fool started. Mostly.

alberto.feel: The grieving son in sunglasses indoors: one dampened cello note, bowed and re-bowed like a number redialed nineteen times. It falls a step and comes back. Nothing resolves.

anya.feel: The recorded voice in Elicia's archive — never present, always heard. An almost-melody that wavers under the tape hiss, never quite stepping forward.

bbs_caller.feel: The sysop of ember.ash.rest.bbs: a modem handshake turned into a figure — chirp, answer, carrier — under a low fluorescent buzz.

bus_kid.feel: The helper: a bright wood-block tap and a smile of brass that climbs a major triad and lands happy.

elicia.feel: The High Priestess at the console: cassette-spool noise and a soft sustained voice-tone (no words) — a fifth up, then settling onto the minor third. She listens more than she sings.

frasier.feel: The Magician at the workbench: a methodical climb in stacked thirds, one piece placed at a time, then the last piece set a step short. A ring-modulated tone with the pen scratch behind it.

john.feel: The Fool behind the counter: an apron-tied phrase on a single mid-range pad, falling to the tonic and holding, a slow heartbeat below. It comes back at the World.

line_cook.feel: The cook at the pass: one brass bell strike, then the heat-vent hum and a two-note call — order up — that drops a fifth.

mackenzie.feel: The Lovers at the receiver: a single piano left-hand figure — root, fifth, octave, back — under phone-line static, patient and a little stuck.

maya.feel: Nine years old, mid-card-trick at booth 6: a ten-second music-box loop in lydian that lands somewhere slightly different each pass — the trick.

the_demon.feel: The man at the bar: a cold sine pad that sits a half-step off everything around it — the phrygian b2 leaned on and never resolved. His key is F against the volume's E.

birdwatcher.feel: The woman in the windbreaker at the river window: a far two-note call on breathy flute, a long wait, one more. Chair creak and a patient exhale around it.

college_friend.feel: An old laugh far in the back of the cathedral — a quick falling figure on distant horns that remembers the year you stopped speaking.

critic.feel: Pen on notebook, a sharp inhale through the nose: two dry harpsichord plucks and a verdict. No music underneath.

drifter.feel: The threshold figure at the bay: gravel, a far match-strike, two slid dobro notes. He doesn't stay long enough to leave a melody.

drunk_uncle.feel: The uncle who arrived and will not be greeted: a sloppy Wurlitzer figure on off-grid steps, a thump that refuses to sync, a glass set down on wood.

superfan.feel: Too-fast breath, paper bag, plastic-cup tap: an eager glockenspiel run that hasn't read the room.

twins.feel: Two of the same tone, milliseconds apart, hard left and hard right — every note of their figure struck twice, a sixteenth apart. They share patience; they share a theme.

vol5_alberto_theme.feel: One dampened cello note, bowed and re-bowed — the grieving son indoors in sunglasses. A fretless pedal enters once and leaves.

vol5_anya_theme.feel: Found-tape hiss on top; Anya's almost-melody wavers just under the noise floor — keep the theremin ducked beneath the hiss, never a clean statement.

vol5_bbs_caller_theme.feel: A modem handshake becomes a figure: FM chirps and chip arpeggios over a low fluorescent buzz. Phosphor green, 2400 baud, no drums.

vol5_bus_kid_theme.feel: A bright wood-block tap and a smile of brass — the helper clearing booths at a skip. Folk two-step in E major, the friendliest thing in the diner.

vol5_elicia_theme_solo.feel: Cassette-spool noise and a soft sustained voice-tone (no vocal) — the Priestess alone at the console, a hymn with no words. The spool runs out at the end.

vol5_frasier_theme_solo.feel: Frasier's notebook: a harpsichord pulse and his ring-tone figure climbing, the warehouse drone behind — distinct from the chapter bed (a working pulse, not a hum). Pen scratch implied by the dry pluck.

vol5_john_theme.feel: An apron-tied phrase on a single mid-range pad, a felt-kick heartbeat below. John wiping the same spot of formica, kindly. The gentlest theme in the volume.

vol5_line_cook_theme.feel: A single brass bell strike at the start, then the heat-vent hum and a slow dub pulse from the line. Work music for a hot kitchen at 4 a.m.

vol5_mackenzie_theme.feel: Phone-line static and a single piano left-hand figure, turning. Mackenzie holding the receiver; when the scene leans in, a velvet pad and upright join under her hand.

vol5_maya_theme.feel: A music-box loop, ten seconds long (three bars at 72), slightly varied each pass — the card trick that lands somewhere new every time. Nothing else.

vol5_the_demon_theme.feel: A cold sine pad a half-step out of tune with everything — F phrygian set against the volume's E, the b2 leaned on and never resolved. The lean man at the empty stool.

vol5_birdwatcher_theme.feel: Chair creak, binocular-strap rustle, a slow patient exhale; a far two-note flute call over the river wind, then a long wait. Almost all room.

vol5_college_friend_theme.feel: An old laugh far in the back of the cathedral: distant horns falling, organ swell, a reverse swell like a memory turning up. The year you stopped speaking.

vol5_critic_theme.feel: Pen-on-notebook scratch and a sharp inhale through the nose — two dry harpsichord plucks and a verdict. No music underneath: no chords, no bass, no pad.

vol5_drifter_theme.feel: Gravel under boot, a far-away match-strike, two slid dobro notes and gone. He doesn't stay long enough to leave a melody — keep it short.

vol5_drunk_uncle_theme.feel: A back-room thump that refuses to sync — the Wurlitzer figure lands on off-grid steps against a boom-bap pocket. A glass set down on wood. Nobody greets him.

vol5_superfan_theme.feel: Too-fast breath, paper bag, plastic-cup tap: a drum & bass tempo in a quiet diner, a glockenspiel run that hasn't read the room. Over before anyone can say so.

vol5_twins_theme.feel: Two of the same tone, played a hair apart, hard left and hard right — a minimalist phase piece on two pure whistles over bowed glass. Patient, shared, unhurried.

vol5_ambient.feel: D'Ambrosio's at dawn — open 24 hours, technically. Brushed jazz trio at a crawl, vibes carrying John's apron phrase, a Wurlitzer, the ballast hum and the bell at the pass.

vol5_warehouse_drone.feel: The Cathedral of Rust and Code: bowed metal and a crypt choir over the riverboat-engine drone, fluorescent buzz, Frasier's ring-tone figure surfacing like a program waking.

vol5_cicadas_dusk.feel: The bungalow at dusk, cicadas through the screen: a dragging trip-hop beat, tape EP, fretless, Elicia's voice-tone. Swings hard — the beat and bass carry the high-intensity stems.

vol5_riverboat_drone.feel: Nicola's dining room afloat: chamber strings and a clarinet over the engine, a radio's static blooming at the edges, a water glass touched at Table 17. Warm, and moored over something dark.

vol5_faucet_metronome.feel: The Roberts kitchen before school: marimba drips keep time like the faucet, Mackenzie's left-hand figure on felt piano, two people deciding again not to fix it.

vol5_two_speeds.feel: Antonio's hot office: a motorik pulse that wants to drive against half-time pads that won't, the window unit losing, the voicemail light blinking. Gone, and about to be gone.

vol5_the_score.feel: A New Orleans bar in refrains: tenor sax over Rhodes and upright, horns behind, vinyl crackle, smoke curling back on itself. The beast not conquered — known.

vol5_lantern_for_those_below.feel: Wind through scrawled walls in the Graustark ruins; one lonesome whistle and a lantern flame, a horizon drone. Joanna raising a light for whoever is still climbing.

vol5_closing_arguments.feel: A Houston law office after the motion is denied: slow noir walk, felt piano, fluorescent hum, files squared with a knock — Alberto's cello note turning over and over. The wheel turns either way.

vol5_the_weighing.feel: Erica Campbell's next morning, office to studio: chamber strings in harmonic minor, a clarinet weighing two lines against each other, a clock. The scales don't lie about the cost.

vol5_gravity_optional.feel: Natalie's apartment after midnight: a slow trip-hop drag, celesta floating in lydian, incense and tape hiss, reverse swells — the world seen calmly upside down.

vol5_the_quiet_floor.feel: St. Jude's Mercy hospice, the last Tuesday in April: a hymn at the pace of the breathing machines, felt piano, choir far down the hall. Nothing exempt, nothing cruel.

vol5_moderate_tuesday.feel: A Montreal apartment years on: a jazz trio in patient exchange, vibes answering felt piano like two cups passed across a table. Nothing spills.

vol5_gumbo_limbo.feel: Jimmy Daigle under a wobbling ceiling fan: a swamp groove, harmonica bending the Demon's half-step figure, Wurlitzer, fretless. The chains are loose. The chains stay on.

vol5_render_queue.feel: Elicia's command center gone to plaster: industrial at full fan load, her voice-figure through a blown speaker, Reese bass, impacts — the crown already airborne. Stems for the collapse.

vol5_glass_skin.feel: Graustark ruins under a shard-of-mirror moon: harp over bowed glass and shimmer in D lydian, water poured onto the earth, glass pings. Ink drying on glass skin.

vol5_five_am_reading.feel: After the cards, before the sun: a celesta lullaby in C# minor over crickets and a parlor clock, Nicola asleep, Aria gone quiet (which is different). The softest stems in the volume.

vol5_saint_viateur.feel: Café Olimpico, late May: nylon guitar and Wurlitzer in A major, espresso clatter, cups. Six years of Tuesdays; by now the staff just nod. Plain sunshine.

vol5_the_stillness_breaks.feel: One Tuesday morning across Graustark: post-rock from wind and shimmer up to full band, brass calling, the hush shattering like flawed glass. The stems are the arrival.

vol5_minstrals_green.feel: Down by the river where the steamship rusts: a bayou porch tune in E major, flute carrying John's apron phrase home, nylon and cicadas, a stick tapping a crawdad hole. The Frog says: mostly.

vol5_noon_room_room.feel: Lunch-rush jukebox B-side: a Lake Charles dance-floor two-step, reeds where the accordion would be, organ and brass mic'd hot, the cook's order-up figure in the hook.

vol5_where_the_bar_used_to_be.feel: Evening-service jukebox B-side: solo after-hours piano recorded in the diner in 1979 — felt piano only, both hands, vinyl age on it. Also the New Orleans bar locale bed in Strength.

vol5_sinking_feeling.feel: Magician · easy. Afternoon sun on the cathedral skylights, low river lap outside, a distant freight horn on french horn. The riverside knowing what's coming and not saying.

vol5_watch_party.feel: Magician · medium, 9:30 PM. TV-room hum, the Pomegranate Hour theme (Elicia's figure, lo-fi and muffled) bleeding through one wall, a far laugh from someone who isn't supposed to be there.

vol5_blow_out_the_candles.feel: Magician · hard, 11:47 PM. Full moon over the river: a distant rager's four-on-the-floor low end through the walls, candle hiss, a theremin above, the bank making a noise the bank should not make.

vol5_cicada_session.feel: Priestess · easy, 9:18 PM. The reel turning fresh as a minimalist pulse; cicadas louder than they should be; the red record-light; Elicia's figure on a Mk I.

vol5_long_quiet.feel: Priestess · medium, 11:02 PM. Confessional hour: a sparse solo piano over the booth's own noise floor (tape hiss and room — no cicadas now), bowed glass far back.

vol5_tape_witness.feel: Priestess · hard, 2:14 AM, off the books. Slow noir in C# phrygian, Anya's theremin figure as the truth-teller already in the booth, tremolo strings, the dark cathedral humming on the other side.

vol5_static_bloom.feel: Empress · easy. Friday dinner on Nicola's riverboat: a Gulf-coast shuffle with clarinet and silver strings, first arrivals setting the long table, glasses touched, the garden deck still in season.

vol5_harvest_dinner.feel: Empress · medium. Late autumn: a slowed folk tune, nylon guitar picking out Frasier's figure as he walks the bank, strings under, wind across a cooled garden deck.

vol5_ice_in_the_river.feel: Empress · hard, 11:14 PM, late February. Ice in the river for the first time in a decade: chamber strings in tremolo, celesta like cracking ice, frost pads, glass pings.

vol5_docket.feel: Emperor · easy. Tuesday morning: a steady boom-bap office pocket, brass clock ticking, harpsichord paperwork, the radiator on too high, a stamp on the blotter every few bars.

vol5_first_session.feel: Emperor · medium. Pre-clerk Monday: a sparse jazz trio, harmon-muted trumpet, cold radiator, frost pad. The petitioner slept in their car.

vol5_appeal.feel: Emperor · hard. Late Tuesday afternoon, six-month appellate hearing, volumes 9 and 10 of the river-code missing: chamber strings in harmonic minor, tremolo rising, the gavel knock.

vol5_green_phosphor.feel: Hierophant · easy. Tuesday night BBS: a synthwave hum, the sysop's handshake figure on a neon square lead, modem rack and banner paper rolling slowly.

vol5_long_signal.feel: Hierophant · medium. Late Wednesday, Anya at the floppy wall, the ham band open at 14.301 MHz: dub echoes, a sub, her theremin figure riding the static.

vol5_broadcast_night.feel: Hierophant · hard, 3:14 AM. The lurker logged in: synth horror in B phrygian, FM lead, Reese, crypt choir; the ham band hisses then clears, a neon flicker.

vol5_demon_filly.feel: A young horse's exhale, a hoof on wood once, then waiting. A low sub pad and room tone; one knock; nothing melodic.

vol5_demon_husk.feel: Hollow corn rasp, dry rustle — the sound of nothing left inside the case. A hollow-body pad and wind; no bass, no melody.

vol5_demon_moth.feel: Paper against a bulb, a glass tap, one high whistling overtone that doesn't resolve — a thin bowed-glass tone held in lydian over the ballast hum. No melody.

vol5_demon_starling.feel: Many small wings, no melody: shaker flutter and a moving séance pad, then a whoosh — the whole flock turning the same instant.

vol5_demon_steamboat.feel: The workbench paddle-wheel, not the river one: a two-bar toy-piano micro-loop in F against the volume's E, a clock tick. The texture is wrong on purpose.

vol5_demon_vagrant.feel: Low rumble, a slow shuffle of bags, distant radio static — a dub sub and sparse shuffled kit drifting through the room, no melody.

vol5_demon_weir.feel: Water under boards, pressure building behind a thing about to spill: tremolo strings and a sub drone under a long riser that never breaks. No hit — it doesn't spill.

vol5_steamboat_motif.feel: The Magician's doom-clock: a slow paddle-wheel pulse and a far steam-whistle that thicken one layer per steamboat-ladder tier (0 → 6) — stems are the ladder. Frasier hears it building whether he works on it or not.

vol5_finale_inertia_fallback.feel: The room sat on him: a tape-wobble pad and sub, motion stopping as the tape brakes, then only room tone.

vol5_finale_maker_breaks.feel: Doubt at max: silence under one bowed pad falling a half-step (phrygian b2 → 1, a downlifter under it). The last breath before the host closes his eyes.

vol5_finale_maker_forgets.feel: Stagnation at max: cassette-deck end-of-tape spool, lights at full — a bright lydian organ chord the cathedral exhales without him.

vol5_finale_river_takes_bank.feel: The bank goes: a building giving up, slow wood-and-metal collapse — bowed metal and a fretless sliding down under a downlifter, one impact, the river after.

vol5_finale_room_walked_out.feel: Three visitors claimed: everything has dropped out except the Demon's cold pad, held alone in his F, half a step off home.

vol5_finale_shift_ends.feel: Midnight, and behind: felt piano and noir strings over the clock, the work undone, the workbench-lamp clicks off. Then nothing.

vol5_finale_steamboat_sails.feel: The steamboat finished: the toy paddle-wheel turns once though no one is touching it, the bank slumps far away (a sub drop), then a held horn tone, resigned.

vol5_priestess_finale_reel_ran_out.feel: The reel ran out mid-sentence: Elicia's voice-tone cut off by the end-of-tape spool. Her hand goes up. The truth lives in the room, not on the tape.

vol5_priestess_finale_listener_breaks.feel: Doubt at max: Elicia in the booth chair, mic on, silent — room tone and hiss, the reel turning; only at the end does her own voice-tone surface, faint. She lets the room record her.

vol5_priestess_finale_session_empty.feel: Stagnation at max: the booked time ends, lounge empty, booth empty — two tired solo-piano chords, hiss, the tape brake. BLANK · don't reuse, again.

vol5_priestess_finale_walked_out.feel: Three visitors claimed: the silences they left, played back through the console headphones as dub echoes and reverse swells. Not nothing. The wrong thing.

vol5_priestess_finale_cicadas_stopped.feel: Cross-arcana collapse: the cicadas stop all at once (a sub drop where they were), the back door open on the dark cathedral, Frasier's ring-tone figure on the other side holding the steamboat. The red light still on.

vol5_priestess_finale_shift_ends.feel: The booth lamp shuts itself off on Elicia's timer: a brushed jazz-trio coda, her figure once more, then the click. Visitors still waiting; she files what's done.

vol5_milestone_bindle.feel: The Bindle assembled in THE LEAP: John's phrase on a lonesome whistle over nylon guitar, the order bell — a small folk send-off. Leap by dawn.

vol5_milestone_candles_lit.feel: A single sustained match-strike, held flame hiss, a low pad. The cake is on the workbench.

vol5_milestone_long_quiet.feel: Elicia's ability: one sustained voice-tone holding a silence that wasn't supposed to be there. A single choir chord as sparse as the engine allows; nothing else.

vol5_gauntlet_win.feel: The Leap (won): a short post-rock lift in E major — John's phrase on brass, strings rising, a riser into the last chorus, the bell. Earned, not bombastic.

vol5_gauntlet_loss.feel: Twenty-Four Hours (reversed): John's phrase in E minor on a dusty tape EP, lo-fi and slowed, reverse swells pulling it backward, the diner's ballast hum left on.
